;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752]]
**After [[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] suggests the plane was downed by an Iranian missile, Iranian authorities reject this theory. Iranian civil aviation chief says he is "certain" the plane was not hit by a missile, still asserting the cause was "mechanical failure". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-51062369 (BBC News)]
*[[January 2020 Quetta bombing]]
**A bombing claimed by the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|Islamic State]] at a [[mosque]] in [[Quetta]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]], kills at least 15 people and injures 18 others, three days after a motorcycle bombing in the city killed two. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/10/world/asia/pakistan-mosque-bombing-isis-taliban.html (''The New York Times'')]

;International relations
*[[Iraq–United States relations]], [[Iran–Iraq relations]]
**Iraqi cleric and Grand Ayatollah [[Ali al-Sistani]] condemns both the United States and Iran over the escalation of conflict in [[Iraq]], saying it shows blatant disregard for Iraqi [[sovereignty]] and the suffering of the [[Iraqi people]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iraq-security/iraqi-cleric-condemns-u-s-and-iran-as-fears-of-wider-conflict-persist-idUSKBN1Z80P5?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*An 11-year-old student [[School shooting|opens fire at his school]] in [[Torreón]], [[Coahuila]], [[Mexico]], killing a teacher and wounding six others [[Murder–suicide|before committing suicide]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/10/mexico-school-shooting-torreon (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019–20 Australian bushfire season]]
**Thousands of people protest in [[Melbourne]], [[Brisbane]] and [[Sydney]], calling for the resignation or ouster of [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]], accusing him of negligence over the Australian bushfires. [https://www.news.com.au/technology/environment/climate-change/major-rallies-held-in-australian-cities-calling-for-prime-minister-scott-morrison-to-be-sacked/news-story/54b61b35563536a0b8a8fade8580b57f (''News'')]
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**Author and [[Self-help|self-help guru]] [[Marianne Williamson]] drops out of the U.S. presidential race. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/10/us/politics/marianne-williamson-drops-out.html (''The New York Times'')]
*The [[Tunisia]]n [[Assembly of the Representatives of the People|Parliament]] votes 134 to 72 to reject a cabinet proposed by [[Prime Minister of the Republic of Tunisia|Prime Minister]]-designate Habib Jemli. [[President of Tunisia|President]] [[Kais Saied]] has 10 days to select someone else to build a new government. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tunisia-politics/tunisian-parliament-rejects-government-coalition-building-must-restart-idUSKBN1Z92EW?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Death of [[Qaboos bin Said|Qaboos bin Said al Said]]
**[[Oman]]i [[state media|state television]] announces the death of the [[List of rulers of Oman|Sultan of Oman]] [[Qaboos bin Said|Qaboos bin Said al Said]] aged 79. At the time of his death he was the longest serving head of state in the [[Middle East]] and [[Arab world]]. [http://news.trust.org//item/20200110233755-nw853/ (Reuters)]
**The high military council of [[Sultan of Oman's Armed Forces]] calls on the [[House of Al Said|Omani royal family]] to convene to name a successor to the late sultan within three days. A three-day period of [[national mourning]] is declared. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/11/sultan-of-oman-dies-state-media-announces (''The Guardian'')]
